title: Nanny Nanny Boo Boo
hook: The playground teasing chant, complete as children sing it: the six-note figure on the falling minor third with its leap up to the sixth, stated twice and ending on a held low note

evidence.summary: Primary: the Wikipedia notation image (SHA-256 4e335b11...), 2/4 in C, sol sol mi la in eighths then sol mi in quarters (G4 G4 E4 A4 | G4 E4). Two statements and tempo from the article's own audio Taunt-simple.mp3 (SHA-256 5cc31d9a...), read with scripts/pitch-track.ts: the figure is played twice at 120 BPM (one 2/4 bar per second), pitches G4 E4 A4 G4 E4 per statement at 392/333/443 Hz, the last E held about 2.7 s. Frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 (recipe.cjs) with two documented preparation edits: a uniform +7 semitone key change (the chant has no canonical key; sol = D5 so the figure lands on unbent buttons, every interval kept) and the final note held a half note as in the audio. Reference: John Wells, Phonetic Blog, "Nuh-nuh" (15 July 2011), an independently engraved staff (ABC G3 E2A G3 E3, image SHA-256 f497053c...): the same G E A G E pitches with the two opening Gs merged, which Wikipedia note 1 also lists as the common five-note variant; a commenter there gives the six-note G G E A G E repeated. The repetition as a second line on the same tune is described by Wikipedia (a second taunt line sung to the figure) and by a commenter on Wells's post (a two-line stanza on the same tune). Wells's MIDI (phon.ucl.ac.uk) is no longer online, so the reference check is contour-level with repeats collapsed.

corpus.notes: Public-domain folk chant with no canonical recording: no original clip kept. The Wikipedia audio is a synthesized illustration, used only for the number of statements and the tempo.
